summary: Mansfield Lahm Regional Airport (MFD) is a joint-use public and military airport located approximately three miles north of downtown Mansfield in north-central Ohio. It is named after Fred Lahm, a Mansfield-born pioneer of American military aviation who served in the Wright Brothers' exhibition team and later became a U.S. Army Air Corps general. The airport is home to the 179th Airlift Wing of the Ohio Air National Guard, which operates C-130 Hercules aircraft alongside general aviation and limited commercial operations.
faqs:
Q: Who was Fred Lahm, the airport's namesake?
A: Fred Lahm was a Mansfield native and early aviation pioneer who flew as a passenger with the Wright Brothers in 1908 and later became a general in the U.S. Army Air Corps.

Q: Does the airport have commercial airline service?
A: Scheduled commercial service has been limited in recent years; travelers should check current schedules as service may be available through regional carriers or charter operations.

Q: Is there military activity at MFD?
A: Yes, the 179th Airlift Wing of the Ohio Air National Guard is based at the airport and operates C-130 Hercules transport aircraft.

Q: How far is the airport from downtown Mansfield?
A: The airport is located approximately three miles north of the city center, typically a 10-15 minute drive.
transport_tips: Rental cars are the most convenient option for reaching Mansfield and surrounding areas, as public transit to the airport is limited. The airport is easily accessed via U.S. Route 30 and State Route 13, both of which connect to nearby I-71. Taxis and rideshare services are available but may require advance booking given the airport's smaller size.
local_tip: If you spot C-130 Hercules aircraft taking off or landing, you are watching the 179th Airlift Wing in action—this is one of the few regional airports where you can regularly observe military airlift operations alongside civilian traffic.
